subject: Latency & error surge affecting Polaris checkout — immediate triage
messages:
From: Priyanka Shah <priyanka@polaris-retail.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwoody.com
Cc: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@polaris-retail.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in checkout failures — p95 latency ~520ms, 3% errors

Sean —

We started seeing a sharp increase in checkout failures on Polaris.com around 08:45 PT. Our telemetry shows a jump in p95 generation latency to ~520ms (baseline ~140ms) and a sustained ~3% 5xx error rate for token generation calls. This is directly impacting payments — carts are timing out and customers are abandoning.

We rolled back our client retry change but still see errors. Can your team confirm whether Redwood is experiencing capacity issues or a model regression? This is high-severity for us — our PM and SRE are standing by.

I attached a small bundle of sampled request traces and a redacted error log. Please advise next steps and an ETA for remediation.

Thanks,
Priyanka Shah
Head of Engineering, Polaris Retail
prianka@polaris-retail.com
+1 415 555 0134

Attachment: polaris_error_snaps_20270530.zip
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.company
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.company, grace_oconnor@redwood.company
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.company, marissa_cole@redwood.company
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Spike in checkout failures — p95 latency ~520ms, 3% errors

Fwd-ing Polaris' report — this is currently impacting production checkout. Key asks: please stand up a rapid triage and recommend immediate mitigations we can commit to the customer.

Quick context for ops: Polaris is on our hosted plan, mixed model pool (gptx-lite v2), steady traffic ~150 TPS during peak. They are on eu-west region but traffic is routed through our us-west edge due to CDN config; that may be a factor.

Immediate questions I want answered in the next 20 min:
- Is this a serving capacity saturation, kernel regression, or model-side error?
- Can we failover to a dedicated pool or warm an alternate model variant without a major config change?
- Short-term customer-safe mitigations (throttling, soft-returns, fallback messaging, temporary cache TTL increases)

I'll take customer communications and exec updates. Karthik, please own technical triage. Grace, please assemble customer-facing one-pager for leadership briefing. Laura/Marissa: we may need approval for a goodwill credit or reserve dedicated capacity if the mitigation requires it.

—Sean
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.company
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.company, grace_oconnor@redwood.company
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.company
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:39:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Spike in checkout failures — p95 latency ~520ms, 3% errors

Sean / Grace — initial findings from the first 12 minutes:

- Telemetry: host-level GPU load on the current multi-tenant pool spiked from 65% -> 92% on the serving fleet handling Polaris' shard. Concurrent KV cache miss rate increased (cold LRU churn) which amplified end-to-end latency.
- Errors: ~80% of the 5xx are model inference OOM/serve-timeout spikes (timeout set 2s), remainder are transient upstream connection resets. No new kernel rollout in the last 24h. No suspicious model weight changes.

Immediate mitigation plan (ACTIONABLE):
1) Redirect Polaris traffic to a warmed dedicated pool (same model family, quantized variant) — estimated 10-12 min to shift routing and warm KV cache. Requires approval to allocate reserved nodes for 4 hours.
2) Lower per-request max_tokens and enforce a 3s client-side retry backoff with jitter — reduces tail latency exposure (can be pushed from our side via per-customer routing policy).
3) Temporarily increase prefix caching TTL to 30s for their typical session flows to capture common prompts.
4) If dedicated pool not approved, enable prioritized batching for Polaris within the shared pool (reduces tail but increases avg for others) — prefer dedicated pool.

Owners: ops_team (me) to execute 1 & 3; infra_team to flip routing (ETA 12m if nodes ready); platform_policy_team to apply per-customer throttling (ETA 8m). Grace to confirm customer comms.

I'll push logs and a short triage note to the incident dashboard: https://redwood.company/ops/dashboard/incident/sg-20270530-polaris

-Karthik
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.company
To: laura_bennett@redwood.company, marissa_cole@redwood.company, sean_gallagher@redwood.company
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.company
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Polaris impact summary & recommended customer remedies (for leadership)

Laura/Marissa — short executive summary: Polaris (high-growth retail partner) is experiencing checkout failures due to a spike in tail latency which we traced to KV cache churn and GPU saturation on a shared serving pool. Customer revenue impact is material during US prime retail hours.

Proposed leadership decisions:
- Authorize temporary dedicated capacity for Polaris for the next 12 hours (cost to Redwood: estimated $7k) to stabilize checkout while ops completes cache warm and traffic shaping.
- Offer a 10% service credit on their May invoice as a customer goodwill gesture if we exceed the 4-hour mitigation SLA.
- Approve a post-mortem + a joint technical review within 72 hours.

Operational commitments we will communicate to Polaris:
- Immediate: traffic will be routed to dedicated nodes within ~12 minutes and we will throttle retries to reduce tail risk.
- Short term (today): stabilize KV cache and monitor p95; expected p95 back to baseline within 30-40 minutes of dedicated routing.
- Follow-up: deliver an ops runbook and recommended quantization profile for their workload by EOW.

Please reply with approval or edits. If you approve, I will send the customer-facing note and draft the credit terms.

-Grace
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.company
To: Priyanka Shah <priyanka@polaris-retail.com>, Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@polaris-retail.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.company, grace_oconnor@redwood.company
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 10:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Polaris status update — initial mitigations underway

Priyanka / Alex — quick update from Redwood: thank you for the traces, they were very helpful.

What we observed: an abrupt increase in tail latency caused by KV cache churn and higher-than-normal GPU saturation on the shared serving pool handling your traffic. This produced increased timeouts and ~3% 5xx observed in your logs.

What we're doing right now (live):
- Routing your traffic to a dedicated warm pool (same model family, quantized variant). Ops estimate ~12 minutes to finish the migration and warm the KV cache.
- Applying per-customer throttling and a 3s client retry backoff to reduce tail amplification.
- Monitoring: Ops dashboard live (link below). We'll push minute-by-minute updates until p95 returns to baseline.

Customer-facing ask: Please confirm whether you can tolerate a ~10-12 minute cutover window. We anticipate p95 to reduce back toward baseline within 30-40 minutes of completion.

We will follow up with an executive summary and proposed credit terms once we stabilize. Apologies for the disruption — we are treating this as high-priority.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.company
